label: forming the future productively: -unga / -ega / -engi and its agreement
note: Chapter 96 supplies the paradigm the point asks for: one lesson per row, mai/tum/vah/ham-ve-aap, with the -aa/-ii gender pair on every form. HALF THE OLD NOTE WAS TOO STRONG and is corrected here. milenge is NOT taught as one memorised farewell: HI-C04-milenge takes it apart, names the root mil-, names -enge as the plural future, and states that Hindi marks the future with an ending on the stem rather than a helper word. What chapter 4 gives is ONE CELL of a grid -- the plural, with no person and no gender -- which is why the point was genuinely uncovered, and the new chapter reads that farewell back as a stem plus this ending. The chapter was blocked on script rather than on grammar: aaungaa and jaaungaa put a long u where the stem ends in a vowel, so nothing can carry the matra and it has to be written as the independent letter uu, which had never been taught. HI-S127/128/129 teach u, uu and o, and aaoge needs the third for the same reason.
